Access today

61 million customers. 716,525 agents. A phone in every hand.

Access is already Nigeria's largest retail bank by customers. Almost every one of them carries a phone, and almost every Closa agent runs their business on one. Today that phone belongs to a telco.

Access has set out to reach 100 million customers by 2027 and 17 million mobile users.16 Access Mobile is built to help hit both, on the device those customers already use every day.

The opportunity

Nigeria's telcos are becoming banks. Access can become a network first.

MTN and Airtel now hold payment service bank licences. They own the SIM, so they own the daily moment. Access already owns the account. A Full MVNO adds the SIM, and with it the relationship the telcos are trying to take.5

Why a Full MVNO

With a Full MVNO, Access owns the SIM, the subscriber, the price and the data. And keeps them in Nigeria.

A Full MVNO sells mobile under its own name on a host network's towers. Access holds the NCC licence. The host carries the traffic. MVNE runs the platform for a fee. This is the model Access asked for on 30 October: no revenue share, and all the net profit stays with Access.

The SIM

Access issues its own SIMs and eSIMs, under the Access name.

The subscriber

Every line sits on an Access customer record, verified once through Access KYC.

The price

Access sets every plan, bundle and reward. No telco tariff to follow.

The billing

Plans are paid from the Access account. Payday renewal and rewards run on Access's rules.

The data

Usage data stays in Nigeria, under Access's keys, with the customer's consent.

Why it matters to the bankEach of the six plans ties mobile to an Access account. That only works if Access owns the SIM and the billing. A reseller deal cannot do it.
Why it matters to the regulatorThe CBN wants payment data held in Nigeria from 1 January 2027. A Full MVNO with Lagos hosting meets that from day one.13
The idea

One Access SIM that grows the bank: salaries, deposits, payments, lending and new customers.

The SIM is not the product. It is the daily touchpoint that brings customers back to Access for the things the bank lives on. Each function below is measured in bank terms, not telco terms.

Customer value proposition

Six plans, each built on an Access product. Same price as MTN.

Every plan answers one question: which part of the bank does it grow? Each one is built on a product Access already sells, so the plan sends customers back to Access, not to a telco. How rewards work

Access Rewards points already buy airtime. On Access Mobile, they buy data on Access's own network.

Access Rewards pays 1 point for every ₦1 on qualifying transactions, and points can be spent on airtime and bills.18 Today that spend goes to MTN, Airtel, Glo or 9mobile. On Access Mobile it stays inside Access.

Customer banks with Access

Card payments, transfers, salary in, savings, on-time repayments.

Points and data are earned

Access Rewards points, plus plan rewards such as double data on payday.

Points are spent on data

One tap in AccessMore or *901#. Data lands on the Access Mobile line.

The cost stays inside Access

Access pays the host network's wholesale cost for the data, not a telco's retail price.

TodayA rewards point spent on airtime is retail revenue for a telco. Access pays full price, and the telco gets the customer's attention.
With Access MobileThe same point buys data on Access's network at wholesale cost. The customer feels the full retail value, and opens AccessMore to use it.

Access Rewards terms from accessbankplc.com [18]. The reward rules for each plan are designed with Access in the Commercial Viability phase.

AppendixRegulation, data sovereignty, technology, Access's markets and MVNE's readiness for Nigeria
Regulatory requirements

Two approvals sit on the critical path. Both start in month one.

The NCC licences the network. The CBN decides where it can sit in the Access group. Both are worked in parallel with the business case, so neither holds up launch. These are points for Access legal to confirm, not legal advice.

NCC

A Tier 2 Full MVNO licence

  • The NCC MVNO Business Rules v2.0 draft (April 2026) set five tiers. DSG's Full MVNO scope maps to Tier 2: Access owns the SIMs, numbering and billing.9
  • The draft benchmarks host settlement: a Tier 2 MVNO keeps 30% of revenue, Tier 3 keeps 40%. The base case assumes 40%, so host terms matter.9
  • Every SIM is linked to a verified NIN, with at most four SIMs per person per network. Access KYC makes this paperless.14
  • 46 MVNO licences approved and 2 live in August 2025. The route exists and is open.10
CBN

Where the network sits in the group

  • The CBN Financial Holding Company Guidelines (2014) need express CBN approval for non-banking activity in a banking group.11
  • A June 2026 exposure draft would bar non-financial investments. Structure is decided early, before the licence is filed.11
Option AA separate vehicle elsewhere in the Access Holdings group, outside the bank.
Option BA subsidiary of the bank, with express CBN approval.
Consumer creditSalary Advance, W Power and LATO offers made on the network follow Access's existing lending rules. To confirm in legal review.
Personal Cyber WarrantyOffered as a warranty with its own terms, supplied by DSG's Digital Resilience.
Data protectionNigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and the CBN payment-data rule. See the next section.1213

Data sovereignty

Every subscriber record stays in Nigeria, under Access's keys

MVNE processes data only on Access's instruction. Nothing personal leaves the country. Access holds the encryption keys, so the data is Access's in fact as well as in law.

Inside Nigeria
Access data centreAccounts, KYC, NIN links and the encryption keys
⇄
MVNE platform, LagosSubscribers, usage, rating and billing
⇄
Host networkNetwork events and interconnect
Encrypted at rest and in transitAccess holds the keysTokenised APIsConsent first
Personal data leaving Nigeria: none

Access is the controllerMVNE is a processor under a data processing agreement, acting only on Access's instruction.

Access holds the keysCustomer-managed encryption keys sit in Access's environment. Revoke them and the platform data is unreadable.

No account numbers on the platformPayments run through tokenised APIs. Card and account numbers stay inside Access.

Consent before sharingCustomers agree in AccessMore before any usage data feeds credit or marketing.

Monitored end to endDigital Resilience managed security across the stack.

Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023Lawful basis, purpose limitation and processor duties, overseen by the NDPC.12
NDPC GAID, September 2025The General Application and Implementation Directive under the Act.12
CBN payment data, from 1 January 2027Payment data to be stored and processed in Nigeria. The design meets it from day one.13

Target design, for confirmation with Access's data protection officer and legal team. Lagos hosting is part of MVNE's readiness plan for Nigeria and is not yet in place.
